author: empire state today
title: Bard College to confer degrees at one hundred sixty-sixth commencement on May 23
text:
Bard College will hold its one hundred sixty-sixth commencement on May 23, with President Leon Botstein conferring degrees to the graduating class. The college announced that it will award 501 undergraduate degrees, 197 graduate degrees, and 46 associate degrees from its microcolleges during ceremonies scheduled for that day.
The event marks a significant milestone for students completing their academic programs across a range of disciplines. Commencement ceremonies serve as a formal recognition of student achievements and provide an opportunity for the community to gather in celebration.
Fareed Zakaria, journalist and bestselling author known for hosting CNN’s international affairs program and writing columns for The Washington Post, will deliver the Undergraduate Commencement address. Zakaria is also among those receiving honorary degrees alongside lawyer Jack Arthur Blum ’62; business owner Patricia L. Bowman; public health researcher Robert E. Fullilove; philanthropist Marieluise Hessel; Bard High School Early College founding principal Raymond Peterson; historian Oliver Rathkolb; physicist Thomas F. Rosenbaum; musicologist Elaine Sisman; immunologist Kathryn E. Stein ’66; and composer Richard Wilson.
Thomas F. Rosenbaum, president of the California Institute of Technology, will give the Graduate Commencement address at Sosnoff Theater in the Richard B. Fisher Center for the Performing Arts earlier in the day. Graduate degree recipients include those earning doctorates as well as master’s degrees in fields such as decorative arts, design history, environmental policy, education, curatorial studies, teaching, music performance and conducting, sustainability management, economic theory and policy, global studies, human rights and arts management.
Several awards will be presented during Commencement Weekend: Olivia B. Carino and Audrey Lasher Smith ’78 will receive The Bard Medal; Amy Bernard ’91 and Matthew DeGennaro ’96 are set to receive the John and Samuel Bard Award in Medicine and Science; Youssef Kerkour ’00 is recognized with the Charles Flint Kellogg Award in Arts and Letters; Kevin Barbosa ’18 and Eva-Marie Quinones ’17 with the John Dewey Award for Distinguished Public Service; Marilynne Robinson with the Mary McCarthy Award; Imran Ahmed ’02 with the Laszlo Z. Bito Award for Humanitarian Service; while Sven Anderson receives a Bardian Award.
Zakaria has been recognized internationally through awards such as India’s Padma Bhushan (2010) and Ukraine’s Order of Merit (2022), along with several journalism honors including Peabody Awards and Emmys for his television work.
Founded in 1860 as a four-year residential liberal arts college located north of New York City, Bard offers bachelor’s programs across nearly forty majors along with advanced graduate study options through fourteen graduate programs.
summary: Bard College will hold its one hundred sixty-sixth commencement on May 23, with President Leon Botstein conferring degrees to the graduating class. Fareed Zakaria, journalist and bestselling author known for hosting CNN’s international affairs program and writing columns for The Washington Post, will deliver the Undergraduate Commencement address.
